title: Coins With the Wrong King
note: After study #202 (Mohamed Bourouissa), prompt MB6: discs fall like slow leaves, flip gold to silver on landing and stack in a neat row; the oldest lifts off when the row fills. Watch first, drag a falling disc to hurry or slow it, drag a stacked disc to toss it back. (Face glyph abstracted to ring vs star-burst, no faces.)

title: The Worried Note
note: After study #203 (Arthur Jafa), prompt AJ1: a single mark plays a nonmetronomic phrase, fast, freeze, replay, slow, freeze, never the same twice; replays leave ghost trails. Watch first, drag grabs the mark but the stutter continues, drag a ghost to erase it.

title: The X-Ray Rowhouse
note: After study #204 (Elissa Blount Moorhead), prompt EM1: five dark house outlines hold wandering light-marks; one house at a time is the bright focus, cycling every 20-40 seconds. Watch first, drag a house to hold its focus, drag a light-mark to move it inside its house.

title: Metaballs
note: Animated metaballs on paper: wandering field sources merge and split as thick black outlines, watch first, drag to add a field source, tap to reseed.

title: Making New Friends
note: Uploaded Procedural IK Cyber-Insect Simulation, as uploaded by Hans: live IK arthropod engine with FABRIK legs, cubic Bezier steps, rotational prediction, panic steps, spring antennae, and a Crimson-Centipede metachronal species.

title: Marble Atlas
note: A procedurally assembled chain reaction across four worlds. Row, climb, swing and roll between connected machines: docking bridges, pressure keys, tipping decks and earned gate releases. Original reactive piano; no final frame.

title: The Last Light
note: A glass ember wakes a forgotten foundry, flowers in a sunlit glasshouse, and constellations beneath a moonlit observatory. One marble, three living chapters, 21 real kinetic acts, endlessly reimagined.

title: Smoke From Nowhere
note: After the Modern Rogue smoke trick: a match strikes low, the flame dies, and the smoke it leaves behind is the piece — curling plumes that bloom, drift, and dissolve, never the same shape twice. Drag to stir the smoke.

title: Five Up, Turn
note: After Salvo Stassi: five balls on a juggler who travels the space, turns full 360s under high throws, kicks balls blind off the foot, and crosses into mills mess.

title: Two Tables, One Marble
note: One red glass marble crosses two tables in a single take: track curves, a rainbow domino line, a blue spinner gate, a seesaw, a gap, and a drop into a star-marked box.

title: Binary
note: A clock told in flipping discs: brass for a lit bit, a ghost ring for a dark one. When the seconds roll over, the flip ripples left through minutes and hours. Tap to hide the digits.

title: The Juggler
note: After Luther Bangert: a juggler in black on a warm stage, five white balls in a true cascade. The hands do the real work — catch wide, scoop low, throw from inside. Watch only.

title: Inkwell
note: Ink dropped in dark water: slow blooms open, curl, and dissolve on a seamless loop. Watch only.

title: Linkwork III
note: Third study after the forged wall sculpture, rebuilt from the chain: crisp rectangular links flowing horizontally, each passing alternately over and under its neighbours. A slow ripple travels the chain; double-tap re-forges it.

title: Linkwork II
note: Second study after the forged wall sculpture: a denser, more tangled cluster of bronze and blackened-steel links. A slow light sweep crosses the metal; double-tap re-forges it.

title: Linkwork
note: After the forged wall sculpture: interlocking bronze and blackened-steel links, hand-hammered, each at its own depth. A slow light sweep crosses the metal; double-tap re-forges it.

title: Pinwheel Quilt II
note: Closer to the hand-drawn original: portrait lattice, stronger swirl, wilder warp. A seamless loop; double-tap re-sews it.

title: Pinwheel Quilt
note: Ink pinwheels on a warped lattice, after a hand-drawn quilt. A seamless loop; double-tap re-sews it.

title: Perigee
note: One closed harmonograph orbit, one traveler. A seamless loop.

title: Gossamer
note: Verlet silk on a slow wind field. Drag to disturb it.

title: Cipher
note: Code-drawn glyphs orbit in concentric rings at different speeds. Drag to stir; double-tap to reseed.

title: Ember Knot
note: Luminous particles stream along a torus knot on near-black, colored like cooling embers. Drag to orbit; double-tap to reset.

title: Interference
note: Overlapping wave fields drawn as a breathing field of ink dots on paper. Drag to drop a stone; double-tap for new waves.

title: Rhizome
note: A root network that grows, prunes itself, and is reborn in breathing seasons. Drag to bend the growth; double-tap to reseed.

title: Split Tide
note: A recursive subdivision that breathes on a seamless loop. Drag to scrub time.

title: Crosscurrent
note: Two ink currents cross an evolving flow field. Drag to stir, double-tap to reseed.

title: Shear
note: Diagonal bars and wedges on a leaning energy band. Tap to flip.

title: Fission
note: Recursive subdivision grid, splitting and healing. Tap to divide.

title: Murmur
note: Luminous particles coalesce into a glowing ring, hold, and dissolve. A seamless loop.

title: Undertow
note: Luminous particles ride a curl-noise current on near-black, drawing the undertow itself.

title: Afterglow
note: Blazing sunset sky over dark silhouette land, thick palette-knife bands, after Jason Anderson.

title: Swell
note: Thick impasto seascape: foam-white horizon over deep teal water, after Jason Anderson.

title: Concrete
note: Hard-edge geometric shapes on a strict grid, slowly reconfiguring. Tap to rearrange.

title: Impasto
note: Thick palette-knife color blocks in a stained-glass jigsaw, after Jason Anderson.

title: Shimmer
note: Dashed rings interfere until the field seems to move; one ring burns vermilion. Click for another shimmer.

title: Compass
note: Needles lean with a seeded weather of direction; the vertical ones turn rust. Click for another compass.

title: Quarter Turn
note: Coin-flip tiles chain their arcs into paths nobody drew. Click for another quarter turn.

title: Warp
note: A checkerboard bulging under two crossing waves. Click for another warp.

title: Hatch
note: One family of lines, swelling and thinning around a hidden light. Click for another hatch.

title: Raster
note: A strict dot grid sized by two rings arguing. Click for another raster.

title: Well
note: Squares turn a little further as they shrink, down a twisting shaft. Click for another well.

title: Solstice
note: A low vermilion sun, warm rays up and cool rays down. Click for another solstice.

title: Orchard
note: Packed canopies from above, big trees first, fruit in rust. Click for another orchard.

title: Alluvium
note: River mouths spill fans of sediment that overlap and settle over each other. Click for another alluvium.

title: Meridian
note: Meridians bend around slow vortices; the strays burn warmer. Click for another meridian.

title: Silt
note: Layers of earth settle, darken with depth, and slip once along a pale seam. Click for another silt.

title: Undertow
note: Rings bent by a slow current crowd into dark bands. Click for another undertow.

title: Faultline
note: The curves are banned: hard turns, bold faults, sudden slips. Click for another fault.

title: Grainfield
note: Twenty-five thousand dots settle where the current bends. Click for another field.

title: Loom
note: Threads strung on nested rings, pulled taut or left slack; gold warps over the weave. Click for another weaving.

title: Driftlines
note: Hairline currents; tone drawn from the water's speed. Click for another drift.

title: Underdrawing
note: The scaffolding first, then the paint. Watch it build, click to rebuild.

title: Hundred
note: A fixed edition of one hundred prints. Click to walk the edition.

title: Crosscurrent
note: Dark and pale ribbons ride the same current and never touch. Click for a new current.

title: Patch Mountain
note: A mountain built from nothing but patches: directional color strokes on a reserved dark ground, no outlines anywhere.

title: Folded Light
note: One palette, three panels, three moods.

title: Marine Snow
note: The dropped 9055s background polished into its own piece: a quiet water column with slanting light shafts, layered drifting marine snow, and a whisper of distant glow. No creature.

title: Meridian
note: Flowing meridian lines in blue-violet. Drag to stir.

title: Dusk Shore
note: A pixel-art beach from above at dusk, drawn with code. The shoreline breathes, wave bands drift, sun glitter twinkles gold, and tiny figures wait at the foam edge.

title: Misregister
note: One geometric form pulled three times in cyan, magenta and yellow, each plate offset like a misregistered print. The color is the misregistration.

title: Weave
note: Warp and weft threads crossing in plain weave. Each thread alternates over and under at every crossing, like real cloth.

title: Ruled Lines
note: Dense hand-drawn rules in ballpoint blue on paper. A hidden field lifts the lines — the ghost of a circular presence you feel before you see.

title: Tidepool Contours
note: A rock shelf at low tide, read as depth bands. The pools breathe, small crabs work the wet rock, and a click drops a pebble.

title: The Shadow of One Letter
note: A red wireframe solid, hand-drawn, casting a shadow built from one repeated dot. The shadow's edge and density do the drawing. Click for another casting.

title: Eternal Bloom
note: Continuous spawn every 2s: squares expand and rotate at uniform rates, alternating direction.

title: Deliberately Uninteresting
note: After Sol LeWitt. Thousands of identical marks; the composition lives in coverage, never in the mark. Up close it is nothing but handwriting, at distance a curve. Click for another field.

title: Square Fountain
note: Hypnotic loop: squares spawn center, grow and rotate, dissolve at max size.

title: What Is Generative Art
note: The artist writes the rules, the machine rolls the dice, and a family comes out. One branching system, six children, one keeper. Click for another family.

title: Smoke
note: One breath, made visible. A single column of smoke rises, widens, and dissolves into empty paper. Click for another.

title: River Stones
note: A quiet bed of river stones, each water-worn smooth, overlaps deepening honestly. One moss-green stone among the gray. Click for another arrangement.

title: Frost
note: First frost on the pane. Ink-blue crystals creep in from the corners and stop, leaving the middle clear to breathe. Click for another morning.

title: Lunar Strip
note: One lunation in twenty-nine moons, waxing to a gold full moon and waning again, each terminator hand-wobbled. Click for another sky.

title: Crows on a Wire
note: Five on the wire and one just leaving. A small moment, drawn plainly, under a big empty sky. Click for another morning.

title: Wind Field
note: A gust frozen mid-passage through wheat, every blade leaning downwind, the bend swelling where the gust is strongest. One red poppy stands unbent. Click for another field.

title: Slat Light
note: Low sun through a fence, the sun itself offstage. Long soft shadows rake across paper, deepening where they overlap, and one warm band falls where a slat is missing. Click for another evening.

title: Square One
note: One square: its sides unwrap into a single line as it turns, then fold back.

title: Unison
note: Continuous spawn every 2s: all squares rotate the same direction.

title: Sides
note: Dot becomes line, triangle, square, gains sides until a circle, returns to dot.

title: Sides II
note: Dot to circle, skipping sides: readable polygons then a quick rush to round.

title: Halved
note: One random polygon. Draw a line through it and every polygon the line crosses splits in two, in tonal steps. Cut as far as you like.

title: Wire Garden
note: One unbroken wire grown from a pool of fragments, bending toward a wandering lure. The wild joints are marked.

title: Trellis
note: Type any word and watch it grow into a hedge, leaves and blossoms along every letter, the word still readable through the green.

title: Flight Deck
note: Seven fogged depth levels of swirling particle trails, flown through like gates. Click to jump to a fresh system; move the pointer to look around.

title: Personal Weather
note: A field of wind barbs, each with a heading of its own. Your pointer paints weather into the air: fast flicks burn amber, slow drifts stay blue. Move your pointer to stir it.

title: Accumulation
note: Sixteen thousand grains of light dropped one by one until a moon, a ridge, a wave, or a forest gathers out of the dust. Click the piece for a new sky.

title: Subdivide
note: A rectangle keeps splitting until every piece earns a texture: hatching, stipple, rings, the odd flat solid. Only adjacent to Mondrian in method. Click the piece for a new variation.

title: Contour Fields
note: Contour lines over imaginary terrain, each drawn a little unsteadily so they read as hand inked. They bunch up where the ground gets steep. Click the piece for a new variation.

title: Mai Menochot
note: A rising sun in two passes of ink over still water, the rust pass deliberately misregistered like a slipped letterpress bed. Click the piece for a new variation.

title: Three Shapes
note: A tangent chain of circles, squares, and triangles in two inks, construction lines left visible. Click the piece for a new variation.

title: Strata Break
note: Concentric rings dissolving from order into chaos, with one red ring. Click the piece for a new variation.

title: Interference
note: Wheels of fine lines turn at different speeds, and where they cross, new patterns bloom and dissolve. This one moves. Click the piece for a new variation.

title: Oscillons
note: Waveforms drawn the way an oscilloscope draws them, layered in phosphor tones on dark. Click the piece for a new variation.

title: Bloom
note: Exact geometry in ink first, then watercolor washes bloom over it and dry where they want. Click the piece for a fresh sheet.

title: Growth
note: A line that follows only local rules grows into folds no hand would draw. This one grows while you watch. Click the piece for a new growth.

title: Murmuration
note: Six hundred particles hold a word that shivers but never lands, until a gust scatters them and they find their letters again. This one moves. Click the piece for a new word.

title: Congregation
note: A living web of three hundred forty seeds that breathes with its own synthesized heartbeat, gathering at every kick. This one moves and makes sound. Click the piece to start it.

title: Tone Mosaic
note: An etching pressed from a thousand voronoi cells, where cell size does all the shading. Click the piece for a new plate.

title: Corridor
note: A quadtree of geometric motifs, camera-projected into an endless corridor. This one moves. Click the piece for a new corridor.

title: Field Notes
note: Wind, recorded the way a field notebook would: inked curves combed across the page, with one red thread running through. Click the piece for a new page.

title: Old Courses
note: An 1881 survey of a river that never flowed, thirteen channels deep. Click the piece for a new survey.

title: Overprint
note: Two ink passes over one quarter-circle grid: indigo first, rust second and a little off register, the way a tired press would lay it down. Click the piece for a new variation.

title: Strata
note: An imaginary terrain sliced like a museum model: translucent elevation layers floating in a dark studio, one warm layer among the ink blues. Drag to look around, click for a new landscape.

title: Tangency
note: A circle-packing study. Discs are placed largest first and grown until each touches a neighbor, so every circle is tangent to something. Rings and arc segments in rust, ochre, and slate on warm paper. Click for a new variation.

title: Lichtenberg
note: A crystal grown from static. Thousands of sparks drift in out of the dark and freeze the instant they touch the tree. Nothing here was drawn, only accreted. Click to grow a new one.

title: Kindling
note: Two fractal flames built from pure density, drifting into each other and back. Bright cores dissolving into smoke. Click for a new burn.

title: Kaleid 99
note: Oscillator bands through a ninety-nine-mirror kaleidoscope, thresholded into hard stripes and printed to near black on paper. One band of color keeps the rest honest. Click for a new variation.

title: Interruptions
note: A dense weave of short ink dashes, each the same length and turned at random, with whole regions erased back to paper. The holes are the drawing. Click for a new variation.

title: Storm Grid
note: Forty-nine nested squares drawn with a plotter's patience, except in two or three cells where the hand slipped. Click the piece for a new plot.

title: Feedback
note: One buffer of noise re-sampled through its own ghost until it settles into flowing grain. The settle is the event. Click the piece to run it again.

title: Still Life
note: Two to four vessels on a low table, drawn flat with long shadows and one accent pot per arrangement. The horizon never lands in the same place twice. Click the piece for a new seating.

title: Hour Hands
note: A clock that repaints itself every minute: three rings for seconds, minutes and hours, each a slow journey between two colors. Click the piece to hold a still.

title: Half-Moon Dots
note: A breathing dotted field crossed by a slowly rotating crescent. Dots that straddle the edge are drawn bisected, so the boundary itself is the subject.

title: What Isn't There
note: A poster printed in reverse: every word exists only as erasure, carved, rubbed and punched out of the ink. Read the gaps.

title: Off Register
note: A playable print-shop instrument: twelve one-gesture motifs on keys A to L, each printed twice with a ghost-ink offset like the sheet slipped. Tap on mobile.

title: Tone Rows
note: A polargraph density study: vertical ticks drawn row by row, length following tone, whites lifting the pen. A rose window in machine handwriting.

title: Orbit Portraits
note: Strange attractors rendered like flame fractals. Every roll picks an orbit; a laciness test hangs the keepers and stamps the duds on the reject wall.

title: Half a Million Grains
note: Half a million grains of sandpaint falling one by one. Nothing is drawn except dots, and the picture emerges. Click the paper for a burst.

title: Own Lines
note: Every stroke is built by hand from shaded triangles, width shaped by pressure, so the line keeps a brush's habits. One study per click: a wave, a heron, bamboo, a grass tuft.

title: Wind Bent
note: Concentric rings sampled through a wind field that pushes in every direction. Click for a fresh gust.

title: Almost Perfect
note: One pen, one line, never lifted: nested squares whose rotation drifts as the path goes in. It draws itself like a plotter. Click for a new hand.

title: Mud Map
note: Three mud zones on the hue wheel, marked dead, and every trapped color drawing its own escape arc to the edge. Click to scatter the colors again.

title: Living Homage
note: After Albers, but the squares never sit still: one slow palette journey, sizes breathing out of phase. Click to mint a fresh journey.

title: Typewriter Weave
note: Struck one character at a time with a shaky hand. Up close it reads as typing; from across the room it reads as cloth.

title: Eye Garden
note: A garden of eye sprouts that watch your pointer go by, pupils widening, then settle back to sleep. Sweep through it.

title: Greedy Squiggle
note: A plotter pen hunts the darkest pixel left on the page, erasing as it goes, lifting to relocate. Mostly one line.

title: Value Ramp Grid
note: Half-square triangles in a deliberate diagonal gradient, light to dark. Nothing else.

title: Bleed Ledger
note: Three hands negotiate on a ruled ledger: hidden pigment, pitted wounds, gravity-drawn streaks. Every trail reads back to its wound.

title: Fifty-Three Divisions
note: The octave divided into 53 commas, brass seams and all. Hover to read each comma in cents.

title: Mark the Seam
note: Twelve pure fifths tiled as kites, the 23.46-cent comma concentrated into one brass wedge.

title: Fusion Threshold
note: Dots accelerate until they stop being dots and become tone. A meter marks the moment.

title: One Series Two Materials
note: One logarithmic series drives both a ribbon's geometry and a striker's rhythm. Same structure, felt twice.

title: Reverse Lookup
note: Drag across a hue spectrum while the piece ranks its palette by simplicity. Vetoes shown struck through.

title: Five Methods
note: One scalar field rebuilt five ways: contour, stipple, hatch, tone cells, drift. Portraits of methods.

title: Face Walk
note: Erv Wilson's hexany as a navigable octahedron. Triads named and sounded in just intonation.

title: Possible Worlds
note: Pascal's triangle as a map of chord worlds. Click a cell to open its diagram.

title: Scale Loom
note: A tuning ladder woven like cloth: fifteen rungs, the pattern re-segmenting live.

title: Hover
note: Marks breathing at the edge of visibility. Your pointer steadies them.

title: Retune
note: Two offset circle grids plus a sheared dot grid. Drag to retune and watch the moire re-resolve.

title: Convergence
note: A tilted crystal of 5-limit harmony. Pulses converge on the root and bloom on arrival.

title: Trough Walk
note: An octave as a washboard of tuning valleys. The probe snaps into troughs; wide ratios eat narrow ones.

title: Held and Shaped
note: Two panels, one material: pulse holds while color shapes, then they trade jobs every 24 seconds.

title: Clang
note: Sixteen agents cycle seven ink marks through a 54-second arc, punctuated by three clangs.

title: Prime Petals
note: A rosette in prime-numbered hues only. Each prime family grows exactly p petals.

title: Tritave Rose
note: Structure repeating at 3x instead of 2x: thirteen rings, marks sized by consonance, slow revolution.

title: Ten Times Exact
note: One recording played ten times byte-identically while the picture turns into notation. Your ears flip before your eyes do.

title: The Exactness Gate
note: Detune the loop by fractions of a semitone and watch song-ness collapse. Exactness as a game.

title: Over Under
note: Seeded Celtic knotwork: strands turn at every wall, crossings alternate over and under, a plaited frame with corner bosses. Click for a fresh knot.

title: Mold and Chisel
note: Fog-sculpture instrument: you place the emitters, the wind does the carving. The last sculpture lingers as a ghost.

title: Eight Minutes
note: This piece only exists during eight-minute fog windows. Between them, a countdown and a tide table of past openings.

title: Seventeen Microns
note: A slider for droplet size against a fixed updraft. Find by eye where float becomes rain.

title: Wrong Octave, Right Key
note: Stretch the octave from 2.0 to 2.6 under a familiar tune. It stays recognizable while the tonic refuses to resolve.

title: Lattice Choir
note: Chords built on a fractional-octave lattice, consonant by construction. Three voices blooming at once.

title: The 3:5:7
note: A brass staircase of thirteen steps to the tritave, lit by odd partials, ending on a 3:5:7 cadence.

title: Master Frequency Only
note: Every sound frozen as a spectral recipe; your only control is one master wheel. Timbre intact, pitch yours.

title: Pairs Only
note: Sixty-four oscillators, spendable in pairs. Rich voices starve their neighbors.

title: Eight Bad Chips
note: Eight synth chips, each with one labeled manufacturing fault. The ensemble of its own failures.

title: Gesture Atlas
note: Draw a stroke and the atlas finds its nearest cousin in the corpus, snapping it under your hand. Endpoints count most.

title: Hue Bingo Canvas
note: Every visit rolls a fresh Hue Bingo palette and lays it down as wobbling colour rings. Coherent by construction.

title: Standing-Wave Hatch
note: A hatch field where a sine wave decides how long each dash gets. Blades of darkness swim through the lines.

title: Family of Blobs
note: The same blob built four ways: harmonic, grown, contoured, implicit. One ink, one plate, the comparison is the picture.

title: Spiral Zap
note: One quiet triadic palette spiralled ten times, calm on the left and feral on the right. The tipping point is visible.

title: Budget Ink
note: A still life shaded on a strict ink budget.

title: Silent Score
note: A polar waveform ring performing a song with no audio.

title: Never Isles
note: A procedural antique nautical chart: radial-noise archipelago engraved as a maritime plate, with rhumb lines, twin compass roses, hachured relief, and recombined place-names. Click for a new chart.

title: Desordres
note: A grid of squares, each disobeying a little; a few burn vermilion. Click for another desordres.

title: Chord Orbits
note: Three rings of points joined every k-th pair by hairlines; one weaves a web, another a slow star. Click for new orbits.

title: Contour Drift
note: Sixty horizontal lines displaced by drifting noise; topographic calm in one ink. Click for a new drift.

title: Night Water
note: Blue-teal motes drift and breathe in dark water; a few wear faint rings. Click for a new tide.

title: Cork Commons
note: The Commons: a riderless horse in flat cork, speckled, standing in clean profile on a plain ground, almost a logo. The public pins notes: tap anywhere on the horse and a small colored note lands with a black pushpin and a short community message, babysitter available, free firewood, lost cat. Around every pin, cork flakes puff off and drift down to settle on the ground. As notes accumulate the horse erodes, edges crumbling near the pin clusters, until the cycle reseeds a fresh horse; the drift of flakes on the ground stays as the memory. Tap the drift to sweep it. It is cork flaking, never flesh: the toll here is attention, and the erosion is the record of use.

title: Fake ID
note: A wallet spills across the table: a driver's license, a membership card, a banknote, a transit card, a library card, flat rounded rectangles with mismatched fields, every name and number invented. Tap the wallet for a fresh spill. Then tap the brass ID machine at the top and watch it assemble a new ID from the spill: the photo slot from the license, the name from the library card, the number from the transit card, the portrait from the banknote, the expiry from the membership card, each field traveling along a dashed line into the cream card. The finished card slides onto its stand and stamps itself SPECIMEN. Tap it to flip: the back carries a barcode built from the mixed numbers. The assembly is the show; watch it, do not skip it.

title: The Notary
note: Alternative Facts, on a green felt desk seen from above: a document at the left, a heavy notary seal on its arm at the center, a silver coin in a dish at the right, an archive drawer along the bottom. Tap the document and a small harmless lie types itself out in typewriter letters. Tap the stamp and it slams TRUE across the lie in red, shaking the frame; at the same moment the silver coin begins to gold-plate, a slow six-second chemical change with pale bubbles rising, no sparkle. Tap the dish and two certifications print: one files into the drawer, one slides toward you. The filed stack grows across cycles; tap it to flip through the lies you have made true. Taps are the tolls.

title: Public Trust
note: A wide black marquee across the top typesets promises letter by letter in white plastic letters, and below it a birch table holds the oath objects in a neat row: a book, a bottle of water, a stone, a small bell, and two linked pinky fingers. The promises accumulate on their own, civic ones mixed with public-figure ones, and the board never clears: when it fills, the oldest drops away as the rows re-set. To add yours: tap an oath object to choose it, then tap the table, and a promise is typeset with that object's stamp beside it while a graphite rubbing of it slides down to you. Tap and hold the pinky icon and the pinky promise posts with a small shake. No text entry: you choose and you witness.

title: The Key
note: Key to the City, as a flat night diagram: a dark city grid with twenty-four locked doors, a kiosk at the bottom dispensing heavy brass keys, and white silhouette citizens wandering between the blocks. Bestow a key by dragging it from the kiosk onto a citizen; the ledger strip at the right edge draws a line recording the reason, for the nurse who, because he waited. Key holders pass their keys on to other citizens on their own, and the ledger keeps the relay. Tap the kiosk to mint a fresh key; keys are never minted for you. Tap any door and a holder's key flies over and swings it open onto its site: a garden gate, a museum door, an ice-cream counter. You must give to receive.

title: Toy City
note: A skyline of toy buildings fills the frame on pale sky blue, and every building is a stack of flat shapes: squares, rectangles, triangles, circles, diamonds, arches, stacked flush with no gaps, roofs of triangles, semicircles, and single diamonds. Checkerboard bands and window-dot grids decorate the wider stacks, and no two towers repeat. The city builds itself one shape at a time, left to right, each shape dropping in from just above its slot; then it holds while the window dots twinkle on and off; then the whole city sinks below the baseline and rebuilds from a new seed. Flat geometry only, nothing casts a shadow. Watch it build. Tap to reseed the city.

title: Alignment
note: A grid of cells on black, each holding four quarter-circle arcs in saturated colors, each cell rotating on its own phase, so the field looks like scattered rainbow shrapnel. Then a wave of phase passes diagonally through the grid and cell after cell snaps into complete circles, a brief moment of total order, before the rotations drift apart again. Two alignment waves cross the loop, and the circles are never drawn directly: they only emerge when the arcs agree. Twenty-four seconds, seamless. Watch for the moment of order. Tap to reseed the phases.

title: The Void Blooms
note: A dark field fills with flat cartoon daisies, rings of six to eight rounded petals around white centers, packed edge to edge in neon pop colors. The flowers cover everything except one clean silhouette: a simple rounded bear head, two round ears and one round head, that stays bare dark ground. The figure is the hole. Flowers bloom in rings outward from the silhouette, smaller and denser near its edge so the outline reads crisp, hold while a few swap petal colors, then fade and begin again. No skull, no face in the void, no shading: superflat flowers and an empty bear. Watch it bloom. Tap to reseed the colors.

title: Detach
note: One amorphous black mass on white, built from thousands of tiny square pixels, and the pixels keep leaving. Edge pixels detach, drift outward, pause, and fly home; the mass slowly breathes between near-circle and oval. Around it float loose colored squares, pink, yellow, teal, violet, that are sometimes drawn toward the mass and sometimes repelled, their mood flipping on a slow timer. Now and then a small white plus flashes inside the mass and a thin black square frame blinks around it. Every mark is an axis-aligned square; there are no circles anywhere. Drag through the mass and you knock pixels loose and push the loose squares; they settle and re-attach after. Tap to reseed.

title: Eight-Spoke Cipher
note: A chart of twenty-eight abstract signs on off-white, seven rows by four, and every sign is drawn from one scaffold only: a circle with eight evenly spaced spokes. Each sign keeps a different subset of the scaffold's arcs and spoke segments, black line art with round caps, no two signs alike. One sign per row breaks the discipline with a single red or blue segment. Faint dotted construction circles show under a few signs, like process slides. Over the loop the signs reconfigure one segment at a time in reading order, then hold: the chart breathes rather than spins. No letters hide in it; a subset that starts to read as a character gets a bit flipped. Watch it reconfigure. Tap to reseed the chart.

title: Noise Halftone
note: A strict grid of circles on white, built exactly in his live order: grid first, shape second, one binary rule third, noise fourth. Each circle's radius is set by a slow noise field, so the grid breathes like a halftone: swells of big circles, shallows of fine dots, traveling diagonally across the field. The one rule: circles left of a slow-swaying vertical divide are solid black, circles right of it are hollow rings, and the divide sits near fifty-five percent of the width. Black and white only, circles and rings only. Thirty seconds and the loop closes exactly where it began. Watch it breathe. Tap to reseed the field.

title: Ribbon Weather
note: Twenty-six circular nodes drift on black, joined by thin translucent curved ribbons. Each node links to its nearest neighbors, and the ribbons arc between them, swelling and relaxing as the distances change; where the translucent colors cross and stack, soft bright overlaps bloom. Now and then the whole web drifts into a loose tangle that almost reads as a numeral or a letter, then dissolves back into weather. Drag and the nearest nodes pull toward your hand, their ribbons stretching; release and the web settles back into its drift. Tap to reseed the nodes. No faces here: the system wears none.

title: Unknown Script
note: An 8 by 8 grid of sixty-four invented glyphs on black, each assembled from the same two part types only: rounded-rectangle strokes, like the bones of a seven-segment display, and dots at the nodes. Every cell holds a different sign, yet the whole field reads as one coherent unknown alphabet. Slowly the script rewrites itself: a wave travels the grid and each visited cell swaps a single stroke or dot, never a whole glyph at once, so the language appears to evolve under your eyes. No letter, no digit, nothing you can read: the meaning stays locked. Watch it rewrite. Tap to reseed a fresh set of sixty-four.

title: Paper Dance
note: Paper Dance: a dark gallery floor with nine closed crates, and a small abstract figure moving between them on a slow choreography, trailing a long ribbon of brown paper that wraps and tangles across the floor as it goes. One by one the figure pauses at a crate and the lid lifts: inside, a small glowing abstract work in a muted primary. When every crate stands open, the works shuffle to new crates, the lids close, and the dance begins again, three cycles of rearrangement. Drag to nudge the figure's path. Tap to open the nearest crate early. Double-tap to reseed the layout.

title: Moor
note: Moor: a rope braided across the dark, and it is not made of fiber. Three strands twist along a diagonal spine, and embedded in the braid are tokens: small abstract glyphs in pink, blue, gold, and dark cord tones, the gifted objects a community gave her to braid with. The rope grows over the loop: tokens stream in from the edges of the frame, fly to the growing end, and braid themselves in. The finished length sways gently. Then, from the far end, it unbraids, the tokens dispersing, and the making starts again. Tap and a burst of new tokens streams in. Watch it accumulate.

title: Horizon Touch
note: Touch: a seascape at dusk, sky and sea built from flat bands of deepening blue, a crisp horizon at mid-height, and strung across the full width exactly at the horizon, a rope. A small dark walker crosses it left to right over a minute, arms waving for balance, torso tilting, legs alternating. With each step the rope dips beneath the walker, the dip traveling with a small lag, and at the dip's deepest the walker's feet touch the horizon line itself: for a moment the figure steps onto the water. A pale glint rides the horizon under the crossing. Then the far edge, and the crossing begins again. Watch it balance. Tap to start a fresh crossing.

title: Licked, Lathered
note: Lick and Lather: fourteen abstract busts on thin pedestals, facing each other across a dark gap in two columns of seven, chocolate on the left, soap on the right. Slowly, each erodes at its own pace, and no two reach the same state: the chocolate heads melt locally, a wandering lick smoothing the silhouette wherever it travels, while the soap heads shrink uniformly, washed down evenly with an occasional sheen. At the end of the cycle all are nubs, then they re-form and begin again. Drag across a head and you quicken its erosion while you touch it. Tap and a wash pass sweeps the nearer column.

title: One Thousand Blinks
note: Butterfly Kisses: a warm off-white field, and an invisible wand wandering it on a slow Lissajous path. At each blink it deposits a fan of short tapered dark strokes, a mascara kiss, eight to fourteen strokes at a time. Over about a minute a thousand blinks accumulate into a dense, delicate field of marks, denser where the wander lingered. The field holds, then gently clears, and the wandering starts again on a new path. No eye, no lash, no face: marks only, the residue of the act. The piece opens on the empty field, the first blink about to land. Tap to reseed the path.

title: Slumber Weave
note: Slumber: on a dark night field, a soft luminous sleeper-form drifts at the left, and at the right a loom waits with its warp threads strung. The sleeper's wandering becomes a glowing trace, and the trace is woven row by row into a blanket, forty rows, each row the shape of a segment of the dream. When the blanket is finished it slides left and covers the sleeper, the cover shadow rising over the glow, and after a rest the cycle begins again: the covered sleeper dreams the next pattern. Ninety seconds, dream to weave to cover. Watch it sleep. Tap to reseed the dream.

title: Hair Mop
note: Loving Care: a dark gallery floor and an invisible mop, fifty-some long strands trailing an unseen handle, soaked in black dye. The mop is yours to drag: the strands follow your hand with a springy lag, spreading and trailing, and wherever their tips travel they lay glossy dye strokes that deepen where they overlap. Paint enough of the floor, past about forty percent, and the room itself begins to back out: the whole field drifts a few pixels away from the dyed ground, the audience retreating. Tap to rinse: the dye fades faster for a few seconds and the strands fall back to rest. At rest the bundle waits at the lower center, a loose dark spray on the bare floor.

title: Gnawed
note: Gnaw, rebuilt at gallery scale: two heavy cubes on pedestals, one chocolate, one lard, and an invisible mouth at work on them. Bites gouge their edges and corners one by one, deepest on the edges that face each other, and every bite pays out in kind: small chocolate hearts appear in a tidy row beneath the chocolate cube, lipstick tubes beneath the lard, made from the removed material. After forty-five seconds of erosion the cubes slowly restore to solid and the rows fade, and the chewing begins again. The chewer is never seen: only the bites appear. Tap to start a fresh bite pattern.

title: Homebound
note: A dark room of familiar things, drawn as thin outlines: a bed, a floor lamp, a table with a cup on it, a chair, all reduced to a few lines each. They are wired together with red wire, sagging runs converging on one small bulb node, and current pulses travel the wires continuously, bright segments on their way somewhere. Every so often one object buzzes: it vibrates for a few seconds and glows a warmer orange, then settles back into the dark. The home is awake and it is not friendly. Tap an object or a wire and a strong pulse leaves from that point through the network. The room runs itself; you just disturb it.

title: Hair Grid
note: A dark textile hanging in space, woven from hair-fine strands: fifty-some warp and weft threads in a plain weave, over and under in checkerboard order, hung from the top edge with a catenary sag that deepens toward the free bottom. A slow wind ripples it in traveling waves, pinned at the top, freer below, and a sheen travels with the bend. At a scattering of intersections sit knots, slightly larger dark points, each with a tiny bright glint that pulses slowly. The weave is imperfect on purpose: a doubled strand here, a gap there, a thread floating where it should dive. Quiet and tactile. Tap to reweave.

title: Impenetrable
note: A square of fine wire hangs in the dark, floating. From a distance, and at thumbnail size, it reads as a soft gray cloud, low contrast, feathered at the edges. Come closer, bring your pointer near, and the softness resolves: thousands of tiny two-prong barbs brighten, lengthen slightly, and glint around your hand. It is barbed wire, and you cannot enter it. Pull away and it softens back into a cloud. The square drifts slowly on its own; drag it and it follows with a laggy swing, then settles home when you let go. Tap to reseed the barb field. No menace beyond the material itself.

title: Undefined Territory
note: A world map drawn in some two and a half thousand small red glass spheres scattered loose on a dark floor: continents with no borders, no countries, no labels. The proportions are equal-area, Africa large and centered, the Americas left, Asia right, Australia below. In the base state the spheres only tremble, a pixel at a time, as if the floor breathed. Tap, and you are the external force: a shockwave scatters the spheres near your tap, they roll outward, and then over twenty seconds they creep back toward home. The territory is disturbed but re-forms, never quite identically.

title: All of a Quiver
note: A tall open steel grid tower, three cubes wide, four deep, nine high, standing alone in a dark room, drawn in wireframe edges only. Every forty-five seconds it loses its nerve: after a calm spell a buckle begins at mid-height and travels up and down, cells deform, the tower leans as much as eight degrees with its stressed edges brightening, holds there groaning, then slowly pulls itself back upright from the base upward, and stands true again. It never falls. A building that cannot decide whether to stand. Drag past it and it leans a little away from your hand, then springs back.

title: Web, Over
note: A monumental spider web suspended overhead, made of fine wire threaded with hand-blown glass spheres at the intersections. Sixteen radial strands run from a slightly off-center hub out past the edges of the frame; sagging capture rings cross them, and at the crossings sit translucent spheres, each with a single small highlight, larger toward the outer rings. The whole web breathes almost imperceptibly, each strand on its own long slow pendulum, the spheres riding their positions, the highlights drifting as if the light moved. Looking up into it, you cannot decide if it is a shelter or a trap. Tap to grow a new web.

title: Hot Spot
note: A steel globe floating in blackness, human-height, barely visible as a dark body with a faint latitude and longitude frame, its continents traced in glowing red wire: the whole planet as a danger zone. The globe turns almost too slowly to notice, one full turn in ninety seconds, the wire ending cleanly at the limb, a ghost of the far hemisphere showing through the steel. It opens on the Atlantic: Africa centered, the Americas at the edges. Drag sideways to spin it yourself; on release it eases back to its slow drift. Tap and a spark pulse travels along one continent wire and fades. No borders, no labels: continents only.

title: Sentence of Light
note: A dark room. Two walls of wire-mesh locker grids face each other across a gap, and between them one bare bulb on a long cord swings slowly on an eighteen-second pendulum, its swing plane precessing so the pattern never repeats. The grids throw huge crawling shadows across the back wall and the floor, magnified, skewed, alive. The bulb itself is small and dim, with a faint warm pool on the floor beneath it; the shadows are the subject, and the room feels like it is breathing wrong. Watch it swing. Tap to give the bulb a fresh push from a new angle.

title: Fragmentos Floor
note: Fragmentos: a floor being laid, tile by tile, with heavy metal tiles hammered from melted weapons. On dark ground, eighty dented, slightly irregular tiles arrive one by one in a slow serpentine sweep, as if laid by invisible hands, each carrying its own field of dents. When the floor is complete it rests, then lifts, fades, and the laying begins again on a new arrangement. You can join the making: tap a laid tile and you strike it, the dent deepens, a flash, a thin ring spreading and fading. Tap an empty cell while the floor is being laid and the next tile is placed there at once, with a strike. No scores, no game: participatory making.

title: Disremembered
note: A tunic hanging from a single nail against a dark wall, woven entirely from raw-silk threads: over a hundred pale horizontal lines with a slight sag. And pierced through the cloth, thousands of tiny blackened needles in irregular clusters, a few dense dark patches in the weave, sparse elsewhere. From across the room it reads as a pale hanging garment; up close it is a field of sharp points. The tunic sways gently from its nail, heavy, on a slow nine-second pendulum, and as it moves a few needles per second catch the light, a brief pale glint, then black again, like dust catching sun. Quiet menace, nothing more. Tap to reseed the needle clusters.

title: Petal Shroud
note: A Flor de Piel: a shroud sewn from rose petals, laid on a dark floor. More than a thousand flat petals, blood-red in a dozen close shades, each with a single darker vein line, overlap across an irregular, fraying outline, and along the seams between them run pale thread stitches, three dashes at a time, suturing petal to petal. The whole surface breathes: a slow wave travels across it over twenty-five seconds, lifting petal edges as it passes. Bring your pointer near and the petals stir and lift toward it, as if the cloth felt your breath, then settle when you leave. No drips, no gore: the red is petal-red, flat and matte. Tap to resew the shroud.

title: Unland
note: Unland: two half-tables, mismatched, their cut edges facing each other across a dark gap, sewn together by hair. Hundreds of hair-thin pale strands arc between the two surfaces, sagging slightly, accumulating over time: a new strand grows across every few seconds, and now and then an old strand snaps and its neighbors tremble. A few strands dangle from the undersides, swaying. The tables are sick; the hair is the suture. Over each minute the web thickens, then resets softly and begins again. Drag across the gap and the nearby strands tremble as if disturbed, then settle. Tap to reseed the cut.

title: Niches
note: Atrabiliarios: a dark wall of twenty niches, each holding what remains of a person behind a translucent membrane stitched into the wall with dashed surgical sutures. Behind the veil, the blurred silhouette of a shoe-like form, some niches holding a pair, some a single form with a darker hollow where its counterpart would be, one niche left entirely empty. The membranes breathe almost imperceptibly, each on its own slow phase. Bring your pointer close and the membrane clears locally, the form inside revealed a little more plainly, then clouds over again when you leave. Quiet inspection, not a button: nothing here changes state.

title: Palimpsest Floor
note: Palimpsest: a floor of pale stone slabs, six by six, that remembers and forgets at the same time. On every slab a glyph is held faintly in sand, dotted strokes along an invented skeleton, drifting slowly in and out of visibility on a long cycle. And on two or three slabs at a time, another glyph wells up as water: dozens of droplets migrate together into a letterform shape, hold for a few seconds, then seep away and disperse. The glyphs are abstract, never real names: the point is the cycle, names forming in two materials at two speeds, one patient and one brief. Tap to reseed the glyph set.

title: Plegaria Muda
note: Silent prayer: the stacked tables of the burial field, seen edge-on as dark horizontal slabs, surface to surface, with bands of dark soil between them. Through the soil, thousands of thin sage-green grass blades grow, sway, die back, and regrow, each on its own slow cycle of growing, holding, and fading, denser toward the middle rows, sparser at the edges. Nothing here is loud: the green is desaturated, the motion is weather. A burial field that tends itself. Move through it and the blades bend aside and spring back, as if you were walking the rows. Tap to reseed the field.

title: Shibboleth Field
note: The 2007 crack through the Tate Turbine Hall floor, drawn as the whole world: a near-black ground, empty but for fine grain, and across it a single fracture system propagating slowly, a main fault wandering with side branches that taper and never cross themselves. Along the freshest edges a faint ember underglow pulses, like heat seen through a fissure, and cools as the crack ages. Over about forty seconds the fault crosses the field; then the ground heals, fading back to plain dark over ten seconds, and a new fault begins somewhere else. The piece opens on the unbroken field, the wound about to happen. Tap to start a new fault at once. Watch it open.

title: Umbilical
note: Her ritual yarn connection, the performance where audience members are linked by umbilical strands: the piece is the web, and the web is the audience. On a black field, small pale knot-points are joined by sagging, fibrous red yarn, each new point tied only to its two nearest neighbors so the web grows organically instead of collapsing into a hairball. It opens with a young seeded constellation of eight points. Tap to plant a new knot and watch its strands draw and sag into place. Drag a point and the yarn resists, sags deeper, follows with elastic lag. Leave it alone for half a minute and the piece begins planting points by itself. Double-tap and the web dissolves into loose drifting threads, and a fresh field begins.

title: Glacier Quipu
note: El glaciar ido, the vanished glacier, at the scale of her hundred-meter quipu acostado. Across a deep cold dark field, long cords run left to right, ice white, glacial blue, raw wool, sagging in catenary curves between four diagonal bamboo spars, dense at the top and thinning toward the dark below. The field breathes almost imperceptibly on a slow cycle. On the lowest cords, droplets form at the belly of a sag, swell, detach, fall, and vanish. And across each three-minute loop the glacier negotiates with itself: a few cords shorten and retreat, their ends hanging free, while one previously shortened cord is restored to full length. No slogans, no text: the melting is the statement. Drag horizontally to send a slow wind wave across the ice.

title: Foraging Quipu
note: A participatory archive that grows while you are away. Twelve cords hang in a dark space, and tied at their knots dangle found objects, glyphic and small: a seed, a dry leaf, a root curl, a wood chip, a petal, a blue plastic fragment, a feather. The first visit shows a base set of five. After that, the piece keeps its own archive in your browser, and on the first visit of each new day it ties on exactly one more found object, up to sixty, with no counter and no announcement: the archive shows itself, it does not report itself. Drag an object to swing it on its cord and watch it turn; everything sways gently, and the bottom of the frame stays dark and empty, because this is the beginning of something.

title: Precario
note: Arte Precario, the rule she coined in the 1960s: structures that disappear. On an empty, sun-bleached shore, small at center-bottom, a fragile sculpture assembles itself from found debris: a feather, a folded paper scrap, a twig, a shell fragment, a red thread draped over all of it, sometimes a pebble, a cap, a leaf. It holds, trembling slightly, for most of a minute. Then the wind takes it apart in the order of its fragility: the thread lifts first, the paper tumbles away, the feather rolls off, until only faint traces remain on the sand. The shore rests empty. Then a new precario, differently arranged every time, begins. Nothing is saved and nothing repeats; disappearance is the rule. Watch-only.

title: Palabrarmas
note: Palabras plus armas: words as weapons, drawn as the things they name. On a flat paper ground, generous and empty like a protest banner, one large word stands at a time, built from hundreds of ink points along hand-drawn letterforms: VERDAD, AGUA, MANO, TIERRA, RIO, FUEGO, LUNA. Over each twelve-second cycle the letters dissolve and re-gather into the object: VERDAD stretches into an eye in blood red, MANO becomes a hand, RIO flows into a river course with banks, LUNA closes into a crescent, then the points stream home and the word stands again. Watch-only; tap to skip to the next word. The word is the mark, never a caption.

title: Blood Knots
note: The Quipu Menstrual grammar: a dense mass of unspun red wool suspended from above, filling the upper two-thirds of the frame. Six hundred sixty tufts of clotted fiber, blood red over rust over dark earth, barely touching, with shadowed gaps between them and longer strands dangling toward halfway down; the bottom third is near-black emptiness, and you stand beneath the mass. It breathes, almost imperceptibly, on a twenty-second cycle. Press and hold to part the fibers; drag to draw a slow furrow; the wool takes several seconds to close behind you, because wool has memory and does not snap. Textile, not violence: keep it slow and heavy.

title: Quipu Field
note: The quipu as a data structure, at room scale. One hundred twenty cords of raw wool hang in a dark void, gathered toward the center like a sheaf, and every cord is a record: clusters of knots along its length, their color a category, their size a magnitude, their position a sequence, an ancient census in a language you do not speak. There is no legend, on purpose: the unreadability is the point. The whole field breathes on a slow master sway, each cord swinging at its own phase. Drag through it and the cords part like walking through the Aran Quipu corridor, swinging aside and settling back with wool-soft damping behind you.

title: Trescientos Sesenta
note: The ensemble's 360-degree format: you sit where the sound gathers. Twenty-four small glyph figures stand on a ring in a dark circular field, no front, no stage, no spotlight. A slow activation wave travels the ring, and each figure in turn emits a resonance ring that shrinks inward toward the center; where the rings converge their light accumulates into a soft interference bloom, and every ring fades before it can touch the exact center, which stays dark and quiet: the listening point, yours. Tap a figure to cue a brighter, faster ring and a soft low tone. Drag in a circle to conduct, and the figures near your hand emit in sequence, a round. Anti-protagonism even here: all twenty-four voices are equal, and the music is the space itself.

title: Marea Roja
note: A red tide, kept planktonic and luminous: a bloom, not a wound. On a full-bleed dark sea, thousands of tiny red cells drift in seven slow gyres, clustering where the currents concentrate them, their brightness set by local density. The bloom lives on a sixty-second cycle: sparse seeding, patches growing and connecting, a peak where ember and glow tones show at the patch cores, then dispersal back to dark water, while a twenty-second breath pulses every patch together. Watch-only; drag to stir the water and the cells scatter, then the gyres gather the bloom again around your disturbance. No fish, no boats, no horizon: just the sea breathing red.

title: Chimba Hue
note: Two banks, two musics, one river. The frame is a vertical triptych: on the left, La Chimba, warm, dense and rhythmic, a field of small bright tick-stars pulsing in interlocking patterns on a two-three-four weave of periods; on the right, cooler and sparser, long slow arcs drifting and breathing; between them the river band, its particles drifting both ways and net down, flecked with foam. The banks are deliberately not symmetrical: they face each other like two choirs singing different music. Drag horizontally across the river and ripples cross the band; when they reach a bank, that bank answers, the left re-phasing its rhythm, the right swelling once. Call and response, with water as the mediator.

title: Thaki
note: Caravan routes as memory. Over a dark land field, pale routes slowly inscribe themselves: thin lines entering from one edge, wandering with mountain switchbacks, exiting at another, while beneath them dozens of older routes fade to ghosts, a palimpsest that builds and rebuilds on a four-minute cycle. Small ember circles mark the pacarinas, the stopping places, accumulating slowly and never cleared. The routes are computed as seeded memory rather than drawn on a map: no compass, no labels, nothing straight enough to be GPS. Watch-only, except that a drag inscribes a temporary route of your own in a breath-shimmer tone; it joins the memory for about a minute, then fades like all the others.

title: Whistling Vessel
note: The whistling-vessel mechanism made visible: sound you can see. A large burnished vessel with a stirrup spout and engobe banding stands on a faint water-table line, its water level showing through the body, and from the spout rises a ribbon of pitch, the whistle drawn in the air. Drag down on the vessel to pour and the level rises: the ribbon thickens, lowers, and curls tighter, and the whistle, if your gesture has woken it, falls in pitch as the air chamber shrinks. Drag up and the ribbon thins and climbs again. Idle, a slow breathing oscillation keeps the ribbon alive and silent. Where No.675 was the physical huaco with its gauges, this is the same ancient physics from the air's point of view: the pitch itself, curling and dissolving.

title: Fifty Instruments, No Solo
note: The ensemble's founding rule as a swarm: fifty small agents on a black field, ten each in five motion families, blowers orbiting in slow arcs, strikers darting radially, rattlers trembling in place, shakers swinging like pendulums, singers weaving long sine trails. Nobody is larger, nobody brighter, nobody gets white. The mass breathes on a sixty-second cycle, each family's density and speed swelling and receding on its own staggered phase, like sections of an ensemble entering and leaving, and the texture is the piece. Drag and the swarm parts around your hand and rejoins. No click, no tap, nothing selectable, by design: there is no soloist here, and there never will be.

title: Combarbalita Choir
note: Lithophony: nine monolithic blocks of combarbalita, the Chilean stone carved with complex internal tubes, standing in a dark field like a megalithic circle. Each rounded slab, pink or mauve, carries its own carved channel system on its face, winding walls and separations, no two alike, glyphs rather than texture. Stone is still: nothing moves until you strike. Tap a block and a luminous ring radiates from the strike point across its face, fading with mineral slowness, while a low resonance sounds, pitched by the block. Tap the same block twice quickly for a harder strike, deeper ring, longer decay. Drag across the row to play them as a sweep. Then silence and stillness again, which is also the instrument.

title: Mapocho Course
note: The ensemble's river-course composition as a living system: one diagonal channel runs from the upper-left, the high Andes, to the lower-right, the city and the sea, and everything is bound to position along the course. The banks change as you travel: snow-blue cliffs at the source, ochre urban blocks mid-course, flat slate at the estuary. The agents morph as they drift: at the headwaters a handful of bright, quick, crystalline darts; mid-river, clumping stone arcs; by the mouth the channel is crowded with heavy, dark, slow swirling disks, density rising exactly as speed falls. Watch-only flow; drag across the water to drop a stone in the river: the swirl travels downstream and the current settles again. No hero, no boat, no labels: the river is the score.

title: Naciendo del Barro
note: His workshop phrase made a loop: quenas naciendo del barro, flutes being born from the mud. On a dark bench, a lump of wet clay rises and hollows as if thrown by invisible hands, never mirror-perfect, its wobble calming as it dries to leather and its finger holes appear. Then the kiln: the whole frame warms, the flute glows from within, embers rise. It cools to burnished clay, and then it sounds: one breathy, imperfect phrase, five notes with visible breath lines curling from its mouth, if an earlier touch has woken the sound; the birth is visual either way. The finished flute fades and a new lump takes its place. Watch-only over forty seconds: a birth to witness.

title: Sotar Condi
note: A memorial: Doblando las campanas, for the Atacama hummingbird deity silenced by the din of the bells. On a near-black field lie the dull fragments of a sacrificed ceramic bell, broken arc shards scattered across the lower half, heavy and still. Above them, barely lit, a small hummingbird hovers on a slow drift, its wings only a blur of ghost arcs, and at the lower right one ember point flickers like an altar candle. Tap a shard and it answers with a dead ceramic thud and does not move: the silencing. The bird keeps its own twenty-six second loop, and once per loop it utters one thin rising cry, quiet, never startling, if your touch has already woken the sound; otherwise the moment passes in silence, marked only by a pulse at its throat. A wake, not a lesson.

title: Del Mapocho al Plomo
note: His Huella Andina cycle as a sounded ascent. One line traverses the dusk from lower-left to upper-right, and the line is the Mapocho: a river meander across the valley floor, then switchbacks climbing past woven textile bands to a snowy peak crowned with a small sun disc, the only text three altitude marks, 0, 2700, 5400 m. Clay offering figurines cluster at three waypoints. Drag along the line to ascend, and the soundscape thins with altitude: river hiss and sparse bird tones in the valley, a soft breath tone as you pass each figurine cluster, rising wind mid-mountain, and at the summit thin high wind and near-silence under the pulsing sun. Release and the height holds, then drifts slowly back to the valley over twenty seconds. Contemplative, never a race.

title: Cuatro Elementos
note: His doctrine as a living cycle, his own sentence made visible: la ceramica es tierra y fuego, porque la greda necesita del fuego para tomar forma; tambien esta el agua que circula en su interior y que, a su vez, activa el aire. Four labeled stations on a thin ring, tierra, fuego, agua, aire, the active one enlarged, and at the center one form morphing in step: a matte clay mound, the same mound glowing from within with a kiln pulse and rising embers, a vessel with water circulating inside it, then the vessel exhaling breath lines and singing once, softly, if your touch has woken the sound. Watch-only on a forty-eight second loop; drag to spin the cycle in silence. A kiln diagram, not a horoscope.

title: Neosincretismo
note: His core term as a morphing profile. One large instrument silhouette in burnished clay with a single engobe contour breathes between two heritages over a forty-four second loop: the European bell, crown, clean curve, flared mouth, and the pre-Columbian whistling vessel, globular body, stirrup spout, chambered interior whose lines fade in as that side arrives. The easing dwells in the middle, where the form is genuinely neither and a gold shimmer runs along its outline, and the small caption beneath fades campana and huaco through each other, both absent at the exact midpoint. Drag sideways to scrub the morph and explore the in-between; release and the slow breathing resumes.

title: Huaco Silbador
note: A whistling vessel, burnished clay with a stirrup spout and engobe bands, sitting on dark ground with its mechanism exposed: two cutaway gauges show the water standing in its chambers. The piece is the instrument and there is no other interaction: drag to tilt it, and the pour begins. Water displaces between the chambers, the air has nowhere to go but out through the whistle, and it sounds, breathy and slightly unstable like clay, its pitch rising from about three hundred toward seven hundred hertz as the displaced-air fraction grows, mist puffing faintly at the spout on each onset. Release and it settles upright, the levels equalize, and the sound dies exactly when the water does.

title: Cáusticas
note: His reel Causticas de luz sobre campana de agua as a loop: los elementos jugando, tocandose, bailando y siendo espontaneos. One large matte clay bell fills the frame, half-submerged, its mouth breaking the waterline at the lower third, and across its body bright caustic light dances as a web of broken refracted lines, computed from an interference field and drawn only where the field crests, never a flat glow. Below the line, its reflection smears and breaks. The water agitation breathes on a thirty-second loop; drag across the surface and the caustics flare and scatter where you touch, the waterline rippling hard, then everything settles back to the dance. Watch, and disturb.

title: Diez Campanas
note: His Al rio Maipo installation as an instrument you play. Ten matte ceramic bells hang over a dark pool, each named for a Maipo mountain: Manquehue, El Plomo, San Jose, Tupungato, Castillo, and five more in the same register, clay lathe profiles with engobe banding, nothing bronze about them. Along the bank rest rounded river stones, your only controllers. Drag a stone up into a bell's mouth and the bell descends toward the water; the deeper it submerges, the lower and fuller its tone, with a wet percussive attack at entry, ripples at its mouth and caustic shimmer lighting its body. Release and the stone falls back, the bell rises, the tone decays. Sound exists only on play, never on load.

title: El Códice Perdido
note: His 1998 tempera series, El codice perdido del Popol Vuh, as an endless codex. Across the middle third of an amate paper ground runs a band of panels in flat tempera and charcoal: a dancer stepping, a sun turning its rays, stacked waters, a bird turning its head, an undulating serpent, a stepped fret, a profile head with its headdress, an invented vocabulary throughout, no copied glyphs, no readable text. One panel only carries a Maya-blue stripe. Each vignette loops on its own phase; glyph dust drifts in the margins. Drag horizontally to scroll the codex, with inertia; it wraps forever. Double-tap reseeds the narrative sequence.

title: Santamaska
note: His 1997 engraving as a living mask. One frontal face, strictly symmetric by construction, its geometry and expression fixed forever; only the line grammar changes. At one pole, Nasca simplicidad extraordinaria: the face in about a dozen bold strokes, one of them cinnabar. At the other, Santamaria locura de las figuras: the same face filled with over a hundred fine interlaced filaments and hooks in charcoal, every stroke splitting and multiplying as the grammar parameter drifts across a forty-second loop, dwelling near each pole. The symmetry never breaks, verified to within antialiasing. Watch-only; it is a mask, beheld.

title: Mujerave
note: LA MUJER CHAMANA: con su vestido de aire colorido, vuela enlazando mundos. A small robed figure drifts across a vast night on a slow fifty-second course, in no hurry, and her dress is not cloth but air: eight hundred particles stream from her trailing edge in four colored currents, turquoise, coral, gold and violet, braiding and curling through the lower two-thirds of the frame on a curl-noise wind. Drag to tear the airflow; her streams shred and redirect, then always re-settle into their braided flow. Tap and she chooses a new route, gliding onto it without ever stopping. She is old, and she is in no hurry.

title: Cien Pesos
note: The coin story: in 1999 a man from the Casa de Moneda asked permission to use his drawing as the model for the hundred-peso coin, and perhaps millions of reproductions have been made. A woman's portrait is generated entirely from engraved contour lines in silver on near-black, nested offset curves tightening on the nose and lips, loosening through the hair, inside a thin copper rim. The medallion turns slowly on its own; drag horizontally to spin it with inertia, edge-on it compresses to a sliver, and every full rotation stamps one faint copy that drifts backward and fades, at most twelve, the reproductions accumulating behind the original. No coin imagery, no symbols: only linework that earns its place.

title: Trompetas de Caracol
note: His 1981 tinta china drawing of Cuasmal musicians' ceramic shell trumpets, as playable ink forms. Four or five logarithmic spirals rest on the paper, ink strokes thickening toward the mouth, each mouth an ellipse with a blush of terracotta inside it and nowhere else; they turn so slowly you would swear they are still. Tap a shell and it sounds: a low breathy tone, the bigger the shell the lower the pitch, between about a hundred and ten and two hundred and twenty hertz, with a ripple ring expanding from its mouth. Sound exists only on tap, never ambient, never autoplay; the audio wakes lazily under your finger. Double-tap reseeds the arrangement.

title: Hace 7.000 Años
note: His reconstruction practice as a generator: one figure caught mid-action in deep time, drawn in graphite hatch on paper under a low horizon, working, never posed. A Chinchorro kneeling over a harpoon in progress by the sea; an Aconcagua hunter waiting with his bow under the hills; a Diaguita farmer bent over a digging stick in the furrows; a Mapochoe musician raising the antara at the river. Each scene breathes on its own small loop, the working arm moving, shavings falling. Bottom-left the caption engine writes its dry pair of lines, hace unos 7.000 anos, and a wry second line for today. Tap and a new era is excavated. Double-tap reseeds the whole dig.

title: Chamán-Cóndor
note: His hundred-by-seventy pencil drawing as a living transformation. Two skeletons with matched joints, a standing man and a spread condor, are interpolated over a forty-five second loop with an easing that lingers in the middle, so most of the piece is spent in the ambiguous country where you cannot tell where the man ends and the bird begins: arms lengthening, feathers growing staggered along them, the torso browning, a tail fan sketching in behind the legs. The head stays human throughout, and its eyes look at you, mirandonos, pupils tracking your pointer; the wings never flap, they ride. Drag sideways to scrub the morph forward or back and explore the in-between; release and the slow transformation resumes.

title: Humo Adentro
note: His doctrine in code: el viaje humo adentro, the inner smoke journey. Four hundred smoke particles curl and drift across the paper on a slow ambient loop, and inside the smoke a face is built fresh from parameters at every reseed: brow, eyes, nose and lips drawn as directional pencil hatch whose visibility breathes with the smoke itself, fading where the field thickens, sharpening where it thins, never fully arriving. The eyes look out at you and their pupils follow your pointer, a face watching from that world toward this one. One small ember point glows low-left. Drag to tear the smoke; the face strains and reforms as the field settles. Double-tap for a new face.

title: Profecía
note: The Condor and Eagle prophecy: two forms of intelligence that split, broke the balance of the world, and are reuniting now. From the top-left a silver eagle, sharp and geometric, spirals inward trailing gold dust; from the bottom-right a condor, a massive indigo stain with pale feathers, spirals in to meet it. At the exact center they merge into a single new form, genuinely neither bird: a cinnabar creature with V-raised wings and a round body that hangs for a held moment and pulses once, before the loop unwinds and the two separate again along their spirals, leaving only their fading trails in an empty sky. Watch-only, forty seconds. No flags, no symbols; the merge is the whole piece.

title: Centauresa
note: Her Wild Woman register: CENTAURESA, mujeres que andamos a caballo, the feminine archetype of freedom. At dusk under flat ember sky bands, a herd of horses runs along a dark ridge as one merged stain-mass of sienna and ochre, no outlines, no separate sprites, backs and necks and heads rising out of the shared body of the herd. Among them rides one woman drawn as a single unbroken bone-white line that never lifts: she gallops her own looping course through the herd, rearing and turning, her trail fading behind her over six seconds so exactly one continuous length of her exists at any moment. Drag anywhere and the line answers your hand, following your path with momentum while the herd parts around her wake; release, and she resumes her own gallop. The rider is the line; she is always riding.

title: Animales de Poder
note: Her mural Animales de Poder as a procession on black. One by one, six power animals emerge from their own stains and cross the frame, each a stain plus a single finding line in its own two colors: the jaguar in rust and ember, the condor as an indigo mass riding high, the whale in deep blue breaching in an arc, the pelican in bone white, the puma in copper and gold, and the goat Amalthea in gold and rust. Each crossing takes its twelve seconds: the stain grows at the left edge, the line finds the animal inside it, it crosses and dissolves at the right, and the canvas breathes empty black before the next. Never two at once. Watch-only, an eighty-four second loop; a procession is watched.

title: La Transición
note: Her Rodin thesis as a picture that refuses to settle: el movimiento es la transicion de una actitud a otra. One horse, built from a single procedural kit, exists only in-between: seven translucent silhouettes interpolated between a gathered attitude and an extended one, ochre ghosts behind, sienna ahead, the middle frame solid iron black, gold dust breathing in its mane. The interpolation sweeps back and forth over twenty-four seconds but is clamped so it never reaches either keyframe: no canonical gallop, no resolved horse, ever, just the frozen transition breathing on pale paper. No blur, no speed lines. Watch-only.

title: Río Bajo el Río
note: Her five-metre EL RIO BAJO EL RIO as a living watershed. A dark ridge crowns the frame; some hundred and fifty streams pour from its springs and descend past three rock strata, and the water itself takes the mountain's colors: rust below the first boundary, copper green through the middle band, granite gray low down, the mineral carried in the ribbon, not sprinkled on it. At the basin the streams land and lay sediment grain by grain, a record that builds and only slowly fades, and under the surface line the same rivers keep flowing in pale gold at forty percent: the river under the river. Drag through the flow to stir eddies and bloom mineral plumes. Tap for a surge of new water from the ridge.

title: Pluma de Sietecolores
note: Their twenty-metre Panamericanos feather as a two-authorship generator, built on two independent seeds. His form seed grows a stone feather: a granite silhouette, shaft and forty-six barbs, fracture facets on its faces, assembling barb by barb over eight seconds. Her color seed then floods it: seven discrete stains in sequence, cinnabar, gold, turquoise, indigo, violet, ember, bone, each a blotchy band masked strictly to the feather, bleeding only where bands meet, never a rainbow gradient, never a drop on the black ground. The colors hold at full saturation, then drain back to the bare gray form and the cycle turns, a new form, a new coloring. Watch-only; the division of authorship is the point.

title: Hanan Pacha
note: Her celestial Andean sky, the Inca upper world: three flat strata of deep blue with ragged drifting edges, each carrying slow gold dust, and below them the dark margin of the underworld, empty. Across the strata a condor PRESENCE glides: not a drawn bird but a wingspan read as lighter mass against the dark, a stain-field of pale blotches with fifty or so individual feather barbs fanning from each wing spine, rippling faintly as it crosses, dissolving back into the sky at the far edge. One small cinnabar disc rides high right, the only red in the piece. Watch-only, a forty-eight second loop; the sky is to be beheld, not used.

title: Mancha Primero
note: Her doctrine in code: la mancha primero, el dibujo despues, the stain first, the drawing after. On pale paper a stain grows unscripted for twenty seconds, dozens of wandering blotches of ochre, sienna and iron black piling into one ragged mass with gold dust settling in it. Then the finding: one continuous charcoal line traces the stain's edge, and inside it a few more strokes discover the animal the blotches were hiding, an eagle in the first stain, chosen from horse, condor, eagle or snake by the outline's own shape; the stain stays as the body. The found animal holds, breathes a little, fades, and a new stain begins. Tap to seed a fresh stain where you touch. Double-tap to reseed the whole family.

title: Hanan Pacha
note: Her celestial world, from his study's network: Leible's Condor and Aguila paintings and the Inca upper world as a flight band. A dark celestial band crosses the frame; six flat geometric birds, condors broad and flat-winged, aguilas smaller and swept, all built from triangles in paper white at varying depths, ride slow thermal loops across it, banking as they turn, wings absolutely rigid, never flapping, never landing. A thin gold ring drifts along the band marking a thermal; birds whose loops pass near it lift a little, riding the rise. Drag and you shift the wind: every flight path bends leeward until the wind decays back to calm.

title: Pila del Oráculo
note: His Oraculo Imperial baptismal font as a stillness instrument: a circular stone font centered on black, a thick hand-cut ring holding a disc of dark water fed, the caption says, from Cerro El Plomo: es agua del oraculo. On the water, one reflected star, a single paper point with a short distorted echo beneath it. The water level breathes on a slow minute-long loop, swelling and settling, the star's echo stretching and relaxing with it. Watch-only calm; drag across the water if you must and ripples spread from your path, the echo trembling, then everything settles back to glass over a few seconds.

title: Forma y Color
note: Their collaboration grammar as a two-pass piece by two authors: Forma F Gazitua, Color Angela Leible. His pass: a stacked-stone monolith in pure grayscale, five flat stones stepping from dark base to light top, fracture wedges on the faces; the form is fixed and never changes. Her pass: stains of exactly three flat colors, iron red, condor gold, sky, bloom from seed points on the stone and spread across its surface following its own topology, cell by cell, until the form is fully colored in crisp territories, never a drop on the ground. Tap the stone to seed one more bloom. Double-tap and only the color is reseeded: the stains clear to gray and bloom again differently over the identical form.

title: Cinco Estrellas
